java-introduction--history-of-java:
JDK 1.0   1996  first public release
JDK 1.1   1997  inner classes, JDBC, reflection
J2SE 1.2  1998  Collections framework, Swing
J2SE 1.4  2002  assert, NIO, regex
Java 5    2004  generics, autoboxing, enums, varargs
Java 7    2011  try-with-resources, diamond, NIO.2
Java 8    2014  lambdas, streams, java.time
Java 11   2018  LTS, HTTP client
Java 17   2021  LTS, records, sealed classes
Java 21   2023  LTS, virtual threads
Java 25   2025  LTS
Creator: James Gosling, Sun Microsystems
First name: Oak (then Greentalk before it)
Original target: set-top boxes and consumer devices
Owner today: Oracle (OpenJDK is the open-source project)
Java has evolved for 29 years in this timeline
java-introduction--four-java-platforms-s:
Java SE - Standard Edition
   used for : desktop, servers, core libraries
   key APIs : java.lang, java.util, java.io
Java EE - Enterprise Edition (Jakarta EE)
   used for : large server applications
   key APIs : Servlet, JPA, JAX-RS, CDI
Java ME - Micro Edition
   used for : small and embedded devices
   key APIs : CLDC, MIDP profiles
Java FX - JavaFX
   used for : rich desktop user interfaces
   key APIs : Stage, Scene, FXML, CSS
Some Java SE modules: [java.base, java.sql, java.net.http, java.desktop]
